contracted_route.why_different: Unlike the /api/v1/meta/* proxy, whose '/meta/' action marker the shared middleware special-cases for auth/verify, the skill data-plane proxy path yields action '' from readAction, so x-tdai-user-key is unconditionally required.

evidence.observation: The header guard itself. It reads x-tdai-service-id via META_HEADER_SERVICE_ID and trims; a falsy id returns respondControlError(c, 400, 'MISSING_INSTANCE_ID') before any downstream access. It then resolves the id through deps.instanceRegistry.resolve, mapping an InstanceRegistryError with code 400 to respondControlError(c, 400, 'INVALID_INSTANCE') and rethrowing anything else. It computes omitUserKey from action === 'auth/verify', requires x-tdai-user-key otherwise (400 'MISSING_USER_KEY'), and only then sets c.set('panelMeta', ...) and calls await next(). Every rejection path returns early, so the guarded route handler - and therefore the downstream kernel client - is never reached.

Derives the meta action by slicing after the hardcoded '/meta/' marker and returns '' when the marker is absent. Because a /skill/* request contains no '/meta/', action is '' there, omitUserKey is false, and the user-key requirement applies - this is what makes the skill proxy a distinct contract case from /meta/auth/verify.

Registers `api.post('/skill/*', validatePanelMetaHeaders(deps), handler)`. The middleware runs before the handler; the handler is the only place that reads c.get('panelMeta') and calls deps.skillKernel.invoke(action, body, ctx). Since the middleware returns on any header failure, a rejected request can never reach deps.skillKernel.invoke.

Builds the standard control envelope via controlEnvelope(code, message, requestId) with request_id defaulting to '' when c.get('reqId') is unset, and emits it through respondEnvelope, which returns c.json(envelope, mapHttpStatusFromEnvelopeCode(envelope.code)). This is the single envelope shape all guard rejections use.

Maps the envelope code to the HTTP status: 400-599 to the code itself, 0 to 200, otherwise 502. A guard rejection with code 400 therefore surfaces as HTTP 400 while the JSON body still carries the envelope fields.

Error type carrying the numeric `code` the middleware inspects. InstanceRegistry.resolve throws InstanceRegistryError(400, 'INVALID_INSTANCE') for an unknown instance id, which is exactly the (err instanceof InstanceRegistryError && err.code === 400) branch that yields the 400 INVALID_INSTANCE envelope.

Canonical inbound header names: META_HEADER_SERVICE_ID = 'x-tdai-service-id' and META_HEADER_USER_KEY = 'x-tdai-user-key'. These are the required headers whose absence/invalidity the contract exercises.

claims.claim: A panel route guarded by validatePanelMetaHeaders returns the standard control envelope and never invokes the downstream kernel client when a required header is missing or invalid: a missing x-tdai-service-id yields {code:400, message:'MISSING_INSTANCE_ID', request_id:<string>, data:null} at HTTP 400; an unknown x-tdai-service-id yields {code:400, message:'INVALID_INSTANCE', ...}; and a missing x-tdai-user-key (on non-auth/verify paths) yields {code:400, message:'MISSING_USER_KEY', ...}. Each of these returns early, so the guarded handler that calls deps.skillKernel.invoke/deps.metaKernel.invoke is never reached.

The standard envelope is fixed and four-fielded: {code, message, request_id, data}. respondControlError always sets data to null and defaults request_id to '' when no reqId variable is set, and respondEnvelope derives the HTTP status from the code (400 -> 400) rather than hardcoding it.

The /api/v1/skill/* data-plane proxy is a different panel route from /api/v1/meta/*: readAction only recognises the hardcoded '/meta/' marker, so on /skill/* the action is '' and the user-key is required (no auth/verify exemption), and only after validation does the handler call deps.skillKernel.invoke. This makes it a clean subject for the never-calls-the-downstream-client contract.

Invalid-instance rejection is driven by InstanceRegistry.resolve throwing InstanceRegistryError(400), which the middleware maps to the 400 INVALID_INSTANCE envelope; any other thrown error is deliberately rethrown (surfaced as a 500 by the app-level error handler) rather than being converted into a control envelope.

conclusion: The header guard on the contracted panel route (POST /api/v1/skill/*) is verified contract-first: requests with a missing or invalid required header (x-tdai-service-id missing/unknown, or x-tdai-user-key missing) are rejected with the standard control envelope {code, message, request_id, data} at the HTTP status derived from the code, and the downstream kernel client is never invoked because validatePanelMetaHeaders returns before next(). The same guard and envelope behavior is asserted for the /api/v1/meta/* proxy for contrast. Supporting dependencies (node_modules: hono, zod, vitest, tsx) are absent in this environment, so the canonical vitest contract could not be executed; an equivalent dependency-free runner that executes the real middleware and envelope modules via Node's module-stub loader passes all 58 checks.
